items.label: f03-parts-table
items.front: How does Morphic store a message with heterogeneous parts?
items.back: One messages row plus rows in a wide parts table with sparse per-type columns (text_text, tool_search_input, ...). Writes delete all parts for the message and reinsert them in one transaction (withRLS when a userId is given); reads map columns back to typed UI parts.

items.label: f01-chat-gates
items.front: List the gates in POST /api/chat in the order they run.
items.back: Trigger/message presence (400), auth lookup, share-page referer (403), guest gate when guest chat is off (401), guest IP limit, search-mode cookie and selectModel (503 / 404 provider), adaptive-for-guests on cloud (401 JSON), then the overall (100/day) and adaptive limits for signed-in users (429).

items.label: f02-fail-open
items.front: When does each Morphic rate limiter allow a request without counting it?
items.back: When MORPHIC_CLOUD_DEPLOYMENT is not "true", when the Upstash URL or token is missing, and when Redis throws or times out (3 s race). That is a deliberate fail-open: availability over enforcement.

items.prompt: GUEST_CHAT_DAILY_LIMIT is set to "0" on a cloud deployment. How many guest chats per IP per day does getGuestDailyLimit allow?

choices.text: 10, the default, since 0 fails the positive check
1, since the value is clamped to a minimum
Unlimited, as 0 turns the daily guest limit off entirely
0, so every guest chat is now refused

choices: 10, the default, since 0 fails the positive check
1, since the value is clamped to a minimum
Unlimited, as 0 turns the daily guest limit off entirely
0, so every guest chat is now refused

items.explanation: getGuestDailyLimit parses the variable and returns DEFAULT_GUEST_DAILY_LIMIT (10) whenever the number is not finite or is <= 0. Zero therefore means "use the default", not "block everyone" or "unlimited".

items.prompt: Regenerating an assistant answer: when are the old answer and every later message deleted from the database?

choices.text: Never; old answers are soft-deleted with a flag
After the new answer has streamed and been saved
Only once the user confirms the new answer, in the chat UI
Before the new answer is generated, inside prepareMessages

choices: Never; old answers are soft-deleted with a flag
After the new answer has streamed and been saved
Only once the user confirms the new answer, in the chat UI
Before the new answer is generated, inside prepareMessages

items.explanation: deleteMessagesFromIndex runs inside prepareMessages, before the model is called, and returns the in-memory slice. If the new LLM call then fails, the old answer is already gone; there is no tombstone or undo.

items.prompt: In uploadFileToR2, which pieces make up the R2 object key for an upload, in order?

choices.text: A random UUID, then the sanitized name with no folders
The upload date, then userId, and a hash of the contents
userId, then chats, the chatId, and a timestamped file name
chatId, then userId, and the original file name as sent

choices: A random UUID, then the sanitized name with no folders
The upload date, then userId, and a hash of the contents
userId, then chats, the chatId, and a timestamped file name
chatId, then userId, and the original file name as sent

items.explanation: filePath is userId/chats/chatId/ followed by Date.now(), a hyphen and the sanitized name, so the user id comes first and ownership is expressed by the path. The chatId is taken from the form data unverified, and the name is sanitized and lowercased.

items.prompt: A request carries the cookie searchMode=deep. Which search mode does the chat route pass to selectModel?

choices.text: none: the route answers 400 for a bad cookie
deep, read straight from the cookie as given
quick, the fallback for any unknown cookie value
adaptive, the mode for signed-in users

choices: none: the route answers 400 for a bad cookie
deep, read straight from the cookie as given
quick, the fallback for any unknown cookie value
adaptive, the mode for signed-in users

items.explanation: The route accepts the cookie only if it is 'quick' or 'adaptive'; anything else becomes 'quick'. The cookie is user-controlled input, so it is whitelisted rather than trusted, and an unknown value is not an error.

items.prompt: For a signed-in user on a cloud deployment, the Redis INCR in checkOverallChatLimit takes longer than 3 seconds. What happens to the chat request?

choices.text: It waits until Redis answers, however long that is
It is allowed, as the timeout lands in the catch block
It gets a 503, because Redis is required for chats
It gets a 429, because the missing count is treated as over

choices: It waits until Redis answers, however long that is
It is allowed, as the timeout lands in the catch block
It gets a 503, because Redis is required for chats
It gets a 429, because the missing count is treated as over

items.explanation: The INCR races a 3-second timer that rejects; the rejection is caught and the function returns allowed: true. The limiter fails open: an outage in Redis never blocks chats.

items.prompt: The client sends isNewChat: true. What does createChatStreamResponse do with the ownership check on the chat?

choices.text: It asks the client to resend the request with isNewChat false
It skips loadChat, and no ownership check runs there
It creates the chat first and then checks who owns it
It loads the chat, and returns 403 if another user owns it

choices: It asks the client to resend the request with isNewChat false
It skips loadChat, and no ownership check runs there
It creates the chat first and then checks who owns it
It loads the chat, and returns 403 if another user owns it

items.explanation: With isNewChat true the loadChat call (and the userId comparison that would answer 403) is skipped entirely. The guide stresses that this flag is client-asserted; what stops abuse is the RLS write path, not this step.

items.prompt: A regenerate-message request names a messageId that is not in the chat. The chat's last message is an assistant reply. What does prepareMessages do?

choices.text: It throws Message not found, and regenerates nothing
It restarts from the first user message in the chat
It appends a new reply and deletes nothing at all
It deletes that final assistant reply and regenerates it

choices: It throws Message not found, and regenerates nothing
It restarts from the first user message in the chat
It appends a new reply and deletes nothing at all
It deletes that final assistant reply and regenerates it

items.explanation: When findIndex returns -1, the fallback picks Math.max(lastAssistantIndex, lastUserIndex), the latest message with either role; here that is the assistant reply. An assistant target is deleted with everything after it. The throw only happens when the chat has no user or assistant messages.

items.prompt: A signed-in user, with storage configured, uploads a 6 MB image/gif as multipart form data. Which error does POST /api/upload return?

choices.text: 415 Unsupported Media Type
400 Unsupported file type (image/gif)
400 File too large (max 5MB)
413 Payload Too Large

choices: 415 Unsupported Media Type
400 Unsupported file type (image/gif)
400 File too large (max 5MB)
413 Payload Too Large

items.explanation: The server checks file.size > MAX_FILE_SIZE before the ALLOWED_TYPES check, so the oversized GIF fails on size first. Both failures are 400 JSON errors; the route never uses 413 or 415.

items.prompt: upsertMessage is called for a message id that already exists. Which part of the stored message changes on that insert conflict?

choices.text: Its metadata is updated, and existing parts are left alone
Every message column is overwritten, and the parts are merged in
Nothing changes, since onConflictDoNothing keeps the row
Only its role is updated; the parts are deleted and reinserted

choices: Its metadata is updated, and existing parts are left alone
Every message column is overwritten, and the parts are merged in
Nothing changes, since onConflictDoNothing keeps the row
Only its role is updated; the parts are deleted and reinserted

items.explanation: onConflictDoUpdate sets only { role }, so other message columns such as metadata keep their old values. The parts are then handled separately: delete all parts for the message id, insert the newly mapped ones, all in one transaction.

items.prompt: An assistant message contains [150](#call_1), and the citation map for call_1 exists. What does processCitations put in its place?

choices.text: The link text [150] pointing at the first result
An empty string; the citation is dropped silently
A [missing] placeholder that the UI renders in red
The original [150](#call_1) markup, left as it was

choices: The link text [150] pointing at the first result
An empty string; the citation is dropped silently
A [missing] placeholder that the UI renders in red
The original [150](#call_1) markup, left as it was

items.explanation: processCitations rejects citation numbers below 1 or above 100 before it even looks up the map, and returns "" for them. Missing maps and invalid URLs also become "", which is why the guide calls the drop silent.

items.prompt: A guest on a cloud deployment sends an eleventh chat today from the same IP (the default limit is in force). Which status does the guest limiter return?

choices.text: 401 with a Please sign in to continue body
429 with a Daily chat limit reached body
503 with a Service Unavailable body
403 with a Forbidden plain-text body

choices: 401 with a Please sign in to continue body
429 with a Daily chat limit reached body
503 with a Service Unavailable body
403 with a Forbidden plain-text body

items.explanation: Unlike the signed-in limiters, which answer 429, the guest limiter returns 401 Unauthorized with X-RateLimit headers: the nudge is to sign in. The guide notes this drift between the three limiters.

items.prompt: On a cloud deployment with Upstash configured, a guest request arrives with neither an x-forwarded-for nor an x-real-ip header. What does the guest limiter do?

choices.text: It rejects the request with 401 until an IP is sent
It is skipped, because the IP comes out as null
It falls back to counting the request per chatId
It counts the request under the key for ip "unknown"

choices: It rejects the request with 401 until an IP is sent
It is skipped, because the IP comes out as null
It falls back to counting the request per chatId
It counts the request under the key for ip "unknown"

items.explanation: The route computes ip as the first x-forwarded-for hop, else x-real-ip, else null. checkAndEnforceGuestLimit starts with if (!ip) return null, so a request with no IP header is not limited at all.

items.prompt: Guest chat is disabled (ENABLE_GUEST_CHAT unset). A signed-out visitor submits a valid message from a page whose referer contains /share/. What does POST /api/chat return?

choices.text: 401 Authentication required, from the guest gate
403 Chat API is not available on share pages
429 with the daily guest limit JSON body
400 message is required for submission

choices: 401 Authentication required, from the guest gate
403 Chat API is not available on share pages
429 with the daily guest limit JSON body
400 message is required for submission

items.explanation: The share-page check (referer includes /share/) sits right after getCurrentUserId and before the guest gate, so it answers first with 403. The 401 guest gate would only run if the referer check passed.
